question: Which of the following diuretics is contraindicated in the presence of cardiac failure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Mannitol" -> "osmotic diuretic" -> "increases intravascular volume" -> "may worsen cardiac failure" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Spironolactone" -> "potassium-sparing diuretic" -> "used in heart failure" -> "reduces mortality" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Furosemide" -> "loop diuretic" -> "commonly used in heart failure" -> "reduces fluid overload" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hydrochlorothiazide" -> "thiazide diuretic" -> "not first-line for heart failure" -> "may be used cautiously" -> 70%
analysis: In the context of cardiac failure, the choice of diuretics is critical. Mannitol, an osmotic diuretic, increases intravascular volume, which can exacerbate heart failure symptoms and is therefore contraindicated. Spironolactone is beneficial in heart failure due to its potassium-sparing properties and mortality reduction effects. Furosemide is a loop diuretic that is commonly used to manage fluid overload in heart failure patients. Hydrochlorothiazide, while not the first-line treatment for heart failure, is not contraindicated and can be used cautiously. Given this information, Mannitol is the only diuretic listed that is contraindicated in the presence of cardiac failure due to its potential to worsen the condition.
